method: Windows Computer Use against the running native workbench, plus settings and runtime-log inspection
passed: Opened the custom binding page and its modal recorder.
Recorded F6 for the emote wheel; settings.json immediately contained key code 117 with no modifiers.
Pressed F6 and observed the central Nice emote and caption; the session count increased to 1 and the runtime log recorded Emote 1459.
Pressed the previous Alt+T binding; the session count remained 1 and no new emote was logged.
Tried assigning Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P, which was already the pause binding; the UI reported a duplicate and kept F6. The application remained active.
Restored the original Alt+T binding using the recorder and checked settings.json.
Confirmed that the existing 96 percent scale and five user-selected emotes were preserved.
Inspected the rendered workbench, optional gold ornament and translucent caption in the actual Windows window.
separate_automated_coverage: Duplicate validation, external ownership conflicts, rollback, pause/resume release, mouse side-button decoding, source-asset hashes, classic pixel regression and optional rendering are covered by --self-test.
